newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia signs power deal with Duke unit.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia signs power deal with Duke unit.

text.p: Indonesia's state power company PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara (PLN) signed a 30-year power purchasing agreement on Monday with PT Citra Kartikadaya, 37.5 percent owned by Duke Energy Group Inc, a wholly-owned subidiary of Duke Power of the United States, PLN said.
A PLN official said the firm would buy the electricity at 6.2655 U.S. cents a kilowatt hour (KWh) from Citra, in which Japan's Mitsubishi Corp also has a 37.5 percent stake.
Duke Energy official Parks Cobb Jr said the electricity would come from a 450-megawatt (MW) coal-fired power plant to be built at Cilacap, central Java, at a cost of about $700 million.
The project also involves two Indonesian companies, PT Bimantara Citra with 15 percent, and PT Kanugrahan Kartika Perkasa with 10 percent.
The project is expected to be completed in the year 2000.
PLN also signed a 30-year agreement to buy electricity from local company PT Bajradaya Sentranusa, the official said.
Bajradaya Sentranusa will build a 180-MW hydropower plant in north Sumatra.
PLN said it would buy elctricity at 7.3946 U.S. cents per KWh from Bajradaya for the first 15 years and at 3.4587 U.S. cent per KWh for the next 15 years.
